page.layout: One page of text in a single column; notes in the right margin. The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Non igitur omnis iustificatio sponsæ in remissione peccatorum ponitur, habet n. & alia ornamēta, & alba vestimēta,Apoc.j. 18. & datū est ei vt cooperiat se byssino splendenti,& cādido.Apoc.19. 8. Byssinū n. iustificationes sunt sanctorū. Quis hæc ornamenta, & iustificationes sanctorū ad passiuā obedientiā tantūmodo retulerit? Apostolus etiā sic docet: sicut per inobedientiā vnius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi, ita per obedientiā vnius, multi constituētur iusti.Rom. 5. 19. Certe Ecclesiā Christi magno bono fraudare conātur, qui docent Adæ inobedientiā actiuā nobis imputari, Christi obedientiā nō imputari. Iā vero obedientia nostra, nisi aliquo modo legi satisfaciat, nō potest esse Deo accepta. Obedientia nostra in nobis non potuit, sed obedientia nostra in Christo poterit satisfacere. Itaq; Apostolus sic docet. Quod impossi-bile erat legi, in quo infirmabatur per carnē Deus filium suum mittens in similitudinem carnis peccati, & de peccato damnauit peccatum in carne, vt iustitia legis impleretur in nobis, qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum spiritum.Rom.8. 4. Apostolus, qui testatur ex operibus legis nullam carnem iustificari coram Deo, ac proinde iustitiam Dei super omnes credentes manifestatam esse: hic tamen iustitiā legis in nobis implere docet. Quomodo a. iustitia legis impletur in nobis, nisi quia actiua Christi obedientia nostra est? aut vt doctissimi interpretis verbis vtar, qā dū nobis accepta fertur Christi obedientia, legi satisfactū est, vt ꝑ iustis censeamur [?].
Sed dicunt isti, qui hanc nouitatem inducunt; iustificationem legis à nobis impleri: hoc est, vt iustificemur præditi ea iustitia, quam lex à

page.notes: Page number 333 and running head CAPVT III. read clearly. Signature at foot reads "2 2" in the scan, most likely "Z 2"; doubtful. Catchword "nobis" is at lower right. The first line starts without an indent, so it is treated as continuing from the previous page. The marginal reference "Apoc.j. 18." has an uncertain character after "Apoc." and is copied as printed. Placement of the notes Apoc.19. 8. and Rom.8. 4. beside their lines is approximate. Heavy show-through and stains in the centre of the page make some words uncertain: "censeamur", "qā" and the mark before "iustis" are doubtful. The word "impleri" in the second paragraph is partly obscured. Text in the scan is long s, rendered here as plain s.
